## Amendments of 2026-10-06 — the security review's entries in full (their fixes are live)

INC-443 to INC-448 were registered on 2026-10-05 with their detail held back (G51: the detail of an unfixed hole never enters the public repository). Their code fixes landed in bundle 6 Part A (turn 2, `2e9562e5`; migrations M9a `20261006005138_b11e2482` → mark `20261007120000` and M9b `20261006010039_22ac0b2a` → mark `20261007130000`, on ethio-prod and ethio-staging) and are published (`a284bc55`, 2026-10-06). The entries above stand; this section adds what was held and closes them.

INC-443 (in full) — the public-surface guard could not see grants written as `EXECUTE format(...)`. `scripts/check-migrations.sh` matched `public.<name>` inside each GRANT statement, so a grant built in a loop as `EXECUTE format('GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION %s TO authenticated', f)` passed unseen; M2's closer loop granted `save_posting_identity` and `admin_update_profile` to authenticated this way and neither was in the allowlist; the guard's floor also left the window's earlier browser grants off the list. All were gated inside (their own `auth.uid()` or permission checks) — a census gap, not an open door. Fix as landed: the guard parses the loop's array and the format grant, with a self-test fixture (`bad-public-grant-format-example.sql`); the allowlist completed with reasons. Status: CLOSED 2026-10-06.

INC-444 (in full) — owner doors wrote a revision row per call with no rate gate. In M5 `set_listing_pin`, `edit_listing`, `renew_listing` and `transition_listing` were executable by authenticated callers, each inserted into `listing_revisions` once per call, and none called `rate_gate`; a seller could loop them and grow the table without bound (degradation under the spend cap, not a bill). Fix as landed: DEC-136 — a new dial `revise` (120 per hour) and `rate_gate('revise')` in SIX doors (the four, plus `mark_sold` and `relist_listing` by the class census), each redeclared whole from the live definition with the one gate line added (M9b); the refusal is `rateLimited` in each door's own style; tests PR-27 to PR-32 (`e2e/posting-routes-dials.spec.ts`). The gate counts only calls that complete (a refused call rolls its count back). Watch item for the review desk's plan: the gate counts a reviewer's or enforcer's transitions too. Status: CLOSED 2026-10-06.

INC-445 (in full) — proof blocks that borrowed real rows. Six proof blocks in the window impersonated or read real rows inside rolled-back sub-transactions on ethio-prod (the oldest account, the first real category or city, the highest-priority real admin, real Ethiopian places — files `2a467fcc`, `2f361c07`, `923dd4cb`, `7a1fd81e`, `f98b5cf0`, `8ea67f86`, `a3a572bf`); nothing persisted. Fix as landed: the migration linter refuses, in DO blocks at or after the floor `20261007000000`, a read of the accounts, roles, places or categories tables that does not name the scratch namespace, with a self-test fixture (`bad-real-row-proof-example.sql`); landed files are never edited. Status: CLOSED 2026-10-06.

INC-446 (in part) — the map tiles route. Its POST wrote one fallback log line per request with no rate gate, and DEC-091 counts those lines. Fix as landed: `consumeRate("map:fallback", <hashed client address>, 60 per hour)` on the POST, with test PR-33. The route's other half is by design and its safeguard sits with the map provider — a usage budget or alert on the provider's dashboard, the operator's optional step; that half's detail stays in the Project record until the safeguard is set (G51). Status: CLOSED 2026-10-06 for the code half; the provider-side step is on the operator's any-time list.

INC-447 (in full) — routes could return a raw database message to the client. `src/routes/api/listings/draft.ts` answered an unrecognised door error with `constraint ?? error.message` as the refusal's detail. Fix as landed: `door-error.ts` (`doorErrorDetail`, `doorRefusal`, unit-tested) — the detail is the constraint name or nothing; by the class census the same change in the publish and photo routes and in six read routes' 5xx bodies; the message stays in the server log. Left as it is and recorded: the admin-only translate route's per-key failed list. Status: CLOSED 2026-10-06.

INC-448 (in full) — a client-side pattern could backtrack polynomially on long dotted input. `src/features/posting/contact-like.ts` — the e-mail pattern (client-side advice only; the door's mirror does not backtrack the same way). Fix as landed: a bounded pattern and a 4,000-character cap on the scanned text, with a unit test on a long input. Status: CLOSED 2026-10-06.

## INC-488 — a changed seed text does not reach the live site while an approved row holds the old text (2026-10-07; Tier B; found while reading the route for D81's label changes)

Defect: the interface's texts are layered — the compiled English, then the compiled language, then the database's approved rows (`src/i18n/provider.tsx` :487–509) — and the store's "Sync keys" (`admin_sync_ui_keys`, migration `c14016d0`) upserts every English key to the compiled text but fills an Amharic row only while it is untranslated or empty. So a corrected or changed English text shows its old wording on the live site until "Sync keys" is pressed, and a changed Amharic text for an existing approved row never arrives by a sync at all: it needs the console's import (the row becomes `edited`) and "Approve all reviewed". No bundle close had carried either step. Evidence (bundle 8 turn 1, the published site's two public language bundles compared with the catalogs, `docs/governance/briefs/bundle-8-live-text.csv`): five live texts differed — English `admin.section.attributes.body` and `admin.translations.col.coverage`; Amharic the same two and `account.deactivatedBanner`; the live store held 579 keys per language against 2,070 in the code. Before the bundle's Publish the executor read seven Amharic rows to import and eleven English keys that differ. Class: a second place where truth lives (the text store) with no step in the bundle close. Fix in bundle 8: the close carries the operator steps — Publish, hard refresh, Admin › Translations › "Sync keys", the Amharic import file the bundle ships (`docs/governance/briefs/bundle-8-am-import.csv`, seven rows), "Approve all reviewed" after checking its count; `docs/features/translations.md` says so. Status: the instance CLOSED 2026-10-07 — the operator reported the import and "Approve all reviewed (7)" done and read the imported Amharic of `auth.telegramSlot` live; "Sync keys" was not named in his reply and is asked again at the next close. The CLASS stays open — the store follows a changed seed without a hand step — in the tidy-up round.

## INC-493 — the test harness reset staging's English texts in one lane only, while the other lanes already tested (2026-10-07; Tier A — the E2E harness; found through R-4's red in the executor's local run)

Defect: `e2e/global-setup.ts` resets ethio-staging's English rows of the text store to the compiled catalog (INC-175), but the block sat behind the maintenance gate — it ran only when `E2E_SHARD` is 1 or `E2E_MAINTENANCE=1`. A local run is neither, and in CI the other five shards, the smoke, email and fast lanes start their tests while shard 1 is still in its setup. So after any change of an English text a local run of a test that finds a changed label by its words failed until a CI run had reset the row, and the first CI run raced. Evidence: the executor's three reads — the row `auth.resendCooldown` (English) held "Resend available in {s}s", approved, before and after a whole local run of `e2e/auth-reset.spec.ts` whose setup printed "maintenance skipped (owner: shard 1)"; then run 37696163167 on `858b2137`: the email lane red on `auth-signup.spec.ts` A-1+A-2 at :148 (both attempts looked for "Resend in"), R-4 a retried pass in shard 2, and the re-run green once shard 1 had reset the row. Three tests build a pattern from that text (`auth-reset.spec.ts` :141, `auth-signup.spec.ts` :146, the nightly's `auth-resend-exhaustion.spec.ts` :66); every other changed label is found by test id. The supervisor's first ruling had said the setup "resets every English row … on each run" — true of shard 1 only (read without the gate). Class: a reset owned by one lane while every lane depends on it. Fix (DEC-160, the prep turn): the block runs in every setup, before the gate, one read per REST page through `readAllPages`, the comparison a pure function with five unit cases (`scripts/en-baseline-heal.ts`); every setup prints the healed line. Status: FIX ON dev `40d99978` (2026-10-08); the local proof printed "healed 0" (the row had already been reset), so the end-to-end proof is the first English label that bundle 9 changes — no first-run red in the email lane or R-4 closes it; DEC-160's rule reads the next five CI runs.

## INC-505 — the feed reads every active listing with no order and no page, then sorts in the browser (2026-10-08; Tier B — the public feed, with Tier A parts in its fix; found with INC-503)

Defect: src/features/feed/use-feed.ts :129–140 select from `listings` with `status = 'active'` and no `.order()`, `.range()` or `.limit()`; ranking.ts :49–65 sorts in the browser. The place filter is a stub (:139–143). Payload and time grow with the whole catalogue (REQ-029). ## INC-510 — version 15's cut-name block split names for screen readers and kept a row of place boxes from shrinking (2026-10-09; Tier B — UI, accessibility; found by CI on bundle 9 turn 15, run 37865593933)

Defect: bundle 9 version 15 (C2m.1) specified CutText as two flex parts — the first five characters, then the rest. Flex items are block-level boxes. (1) The browser's name computation puts a space between block-level boxes, so every cut name had a break after its fifth character: the language menu's item read "Engli sh", and the Amharic-path test failed six times. (2) A flex wrapper's smallest width is the sum of its parts' smallest widths, and the rest is one unbreakable line, so the place boxes never shrank: the location row overflowed by hundreds of pixels at 360 px. The chips passed only because a 45% maximum capped them. Evidence: run 37865593933 (19 gating results, classified in block S59's record); the supervisor's reproduction in the workspace's Chromium. The block was never published. Cause: S133 — markup dictated without trying it in a browser. Fix (bundle 9 version 16, turn 16, `31dc53ae`): CutText as one grid cell. The visible element holds the whole name; two unpainted, aria-hidden size-setters with CSS-generated content set the smallest width (five characters and "…") and the widest (the whole name). The row's label, then its arrows, step aside when it is still too narrow. Proven green in CI on `992b8eb3` (run 37872325911), with the Amharic-path test, PW-171 at 360 and 320, and the four-level row at 320. Class rule: a cut name is never split into separate boxes, and a shared block's markup is tried in a browser for its accessible name and intrinsic sizes before a brief dictates it. Status (2026-10-09): CLOSED — walked on the published site 2026-10-09 02:33Z (a long "Used before" name kept its first five letters; a tapped place box showed no ring).

The entries stay as written; these lines are the later word. ## INC-522 — PW-113 failed in the nightly's serial run: after two pin saves the draft's directions were null (2026-10-09; Tier B bridging into data integrity — a seller's typed text lost; found by the nightly of 2026-10-09)

Defect: the place step (src/features/posting/step-where.tsx) keeps `savedText`, its record of the street and directions the door holds, and every door call restates the line it does not change from it. (A1) The read issued when the step mounts set `savedText.current = found` whenever it answered, so an answer produced before the seller's own save put the older text back, and the next pin save restated the older directions (null). (A2) When that read failed, savedText kept directions null, and the next pin save, Remove or details save restated null over directions the step never read. Evidence: the nightly's failure body (no context, INC-429); the code at `0a0a7687`; PW-178 (A1) and PW-179 (A2). The Supabase client retries a GET after a network error (INC-527), so A1 — a late answer — is the likelier cause of the nightly's failure. Class: a write that restates text from a snapshot older than the step's own save, or text it never read (typed absence). Fix (ruling turn 13; `be21faa4`): a counter of successful saves — a read applies its answer only when no save landed while it was out; a seller-driven call re-reads the text first while it is unknown and sends nothing when the re-read fails. PW-178 green on `be21faa4`; PW-179 (corrected by INC-527) green on `2ab35a33` (run 37940943512). Status (2026-10-09): CLOSED — A1 and A2 fixed and proven in CI (PW-178, PW-179); the order of concurrent door calls is INC-526.

Census (G29): five calls, all in the two files; `oauthRedirectUrl` (auth-service.ts :33–37) encodes the path into the callback's own query and is correct. Fix (D119 turn 1, `1f6b4180`): the five calls navigate by `href`; `safeReturnPath` also refuses control characters; RP-1..RP-3 in src/lib/return-path.test.ts (RP-3 red on the old rule, run first — these ids repeat admin-roles' RP-1..RP-3, INC-536) and PW-182, green in run 37996982043. Class rule: a checked return path is navigated by `href`, never by `to`. Status: FIXED.

## INC-531 — PW-180 read the seller's OLDEST listing as its new draft (2026-10-09; Tier B test; found by CI run 37996982043)

Defect: `const [draft] = await draftsOf(user.id)` (e2e/post-wizard-where.spec.ts :283 at `1f6b4180`); `draftsOf` (e2e/helpers/posting.ts :435–443) returns EVERY listing of the seller, oldest first, and PW-180 publishes a prior listing before step 1, so `[0]` was that prior listing. Class rule: a test that makes more than one listing for a seller finds each one by what distinguishes it, never by its position (G28's sibling). Supervisor slip S149. Status: FIXED.

## INC-532 — signing out dropped the place this browser had chosen (2026-10-10; Tier A sign-out sequence / Tier B shell; found by the operator's walk)

## INC-535 — profile columns writable by their owner outside the identity doors (2026-10-10; Tier A RLS and grants, identity; found by the D106 census)

Defect: `GRANT UPDATE (display_name, avatar_url, preferred_language, viewing_location, notification_prefs, contact_prefs, updated_at, seller_alias, contact_phone, show_phone, contact_telegram, show_telegram, contact_whatsapp, default_post_location_id) ON public.profiles TO authenticated` (`20260810075629_2ff72f7a` :79–94; first form `20260730015333_87dbf472` :40–42) stood behind the owner policy `profiles_owner_update` (`20260730015333` :36–38); the only later revoke was `preferred_language` (`20260901225202` :43). So a signed-in person could write those columns of their own row through the data API, outside the doors that judge them (`save_posting_identity`'s name and contact rules, `20261004011235_18556a32` :895–990). The census on ethio-prod listed the thirteen columns. The red run (38026670798, on `12b3a9f5`, before the staging fix) proves `display_name` was written directly; `seller_alias` was refused there for a cause not identified (not the `name_fold` expression index, not the format check) — S150. No public reader shows a seller's name yet, so the exposure was latent. Every function that writes profiles is SECURITY DEFINER; no client code writes the table; profiles was the only table with column-level write grants. Why the class census missed it: INC-478's census read table privileges, and DEC-148's `table_writable_by_client` counted `has_table_privilege`, which does not see column grants. Fix (turn 8, migration `20261010055801_866d39cd`, mark `20261010180000`, on ethio-prod by the executor's tool and on ethio-staging by the operator): `REVOKE INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON public.profiles FROM anon, authenticated` (a table-level revoke removes the column grants), `DROP POLICY profiles_owner_update`; `security_lints()` redeclared whole with `table_writable_by_client` also counting `has_any_column_privilege` for INSERT and UPDATE (baseline 0 unchanged); proofs C1–C5 (each shown to fail on a bad variant on a local Postgres); PR-43 (the owner's client refused on the thirteen columns, the identity route still saves); green in run 38029368030 (attempt 2). Class: INC-476/INC-478's (a rule moved into a door while the direct grant stayed) in its column form. Its body was kept out of the repository until the fix was live on both databases (G51). Status: FIXED.

## INC-538 — SC-11 passed while every filtered read failed (2026-10-10; Tier B test; found with INC-537)

Defect: SC-11 filtered to ET and asserted the seeded row visible; the query client keeps the previous rows on screen (`placeholderData: keepPreviousData`) while it retries a failed read three times, so the old unfiltered rows satisfied the assertion before the error state arrived. Class: a filter test that asserts a row present can pass on the placeholder; a filter is proven by a result the unfiltered list cannot give, with the read settled. Fix (turn A3): SC-11 searches the ad's unique title, filters to US (expects the empty message, no error state), then to ET (expects the row, no error state) — red on A2's code, green on the fix. Status (2026-10-12): FIXED.

## INC-539 — a dialog opened from a row's three-dots menu could leave the page unclickable (2026-10-10; Tier B shared primitive; found by CI run 38089961758)

Defect: RowActions' DropdownMenu was modal (Radix default), so the menu locked the page's pointer events; its entries open modal dialogs that lock them too; when the dialog mounted while the menu was still closing, the lock outlived both — after the dialog closed with Escape nothing took a click (CO-9, every run, both widths). Evidence: the four CO-9 bodies; a jsdom unit test shows the modal menu sets `document.body.style.pointerEvents = "none"` while open. The mechanism was recorded as a hypothesis (a local reproduction did not lock); INC-541 later showed the same overlap through another path. Fix (the B1 fix turn, `7c3953ae`, at the primitive — G29): `DropdownMenu modal={false}` in RowActions and in Admin › Attributes' own row menu. Status (2026-10-12): FIXED (run 38097283598 green, CO-9 passed).

## INC-572 — PR-33 sent sixty-one reports one after another and ran past its 60 s budget (2026-10-12; Tier B test; found by the flake ledger)

Defect: PR-33 ("the map fallback report is capped at 60 an hour per address") passed only on retry in three runs in seven days (2026-10-08 mobile; 2026-10-12 desktop twice), each "Test timeout of 60000ms exceeded" — the DEC-030 threshold with no incident. Root (read): 61 sequential POSTs to /api/map/tiles, each one `consume_rate_limit` round trip (one atomic `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE … RETURNING`); on a slow staging 61 round trips pass 60 s. Second cause (read): the windows are clock hours, so 61 reports that straddle an hour split their count. Class: a dial test that counts by sequential round trips inside the test budget. Fix (turn C10, `45637132`): the first sixty go ten at a time and the 61st after all sixty have answered; within the last 30 s of a clock hour the test polls the clock until the next hour; every assertion kept, plus "PR-33: not 61 answers". Status (2026-10-12): FIXED (runs 38250004537 and after green; no PR-33 line since).

## INC-579 — a category created in the console was not found by the roster's search for 20 s (2026-10-12; Tier B — the categories console and its tests; found by CI run 38261739605)

## INC-624 — a migration proof that compares a function body's bytes could not pass on ethio-staging (2026-10-14; Tier B CI / migrations; found by the operator's staging apply of bundle 14 turn 3)

Nothing was written by hand: a conditional manual insert of the mark, offered by the executor, was not needed and not run. Cause: the proof's design (S208). Fix: from the next migration, every byte comparison of a function body — in proofs and in census queries — removes carriage returns first (`replace(prosrc, chr(13), '')`), so the plain paste passes; no change on staging (a carriage return does not change what a function does). Disposition: ACCEPTED AS LANDED — a whitespace byte inside SQL, no semantic change (the diff read whole), authored file = applied text on prod and staging; no corrective migration (a redeclaration for a whitespace byte is churn and a third retype); the executor's honesty was right. The process answer is DEC-182: from E2b on, a migration longer than 12 KB travels the FILE route (written by script, sha256-checked; the operator applies from the raw file, staging then prod), 12 KB or less through the tool with the post-apply md5 read-back as the byte check; a third tool-route deviation at any size moves every migration to the file route. Status (2026-10-15): CLOSED, accepted as landed. Class: G43 (exact text is never retyped) — yet the database tool takes a migration only as typed text, so every migration through it is a retype; the second retype deviation after S2's 152 KB refusal.

## INC-675 — one ribbon size cut the longer ribbon words at the picture's corners (2026-10-16; Tier C styling; found by the operator's walk of the published site after bundle 18 turn 1)

Read and measured: the band is 84cqw wide, centred 29.7cqw along the corner diagonal at −30°, and the picture's right and bottom edges clip its two ends, so the usable text run is 51.8cqw at 6cqw letters (8.63em), not the band's 59.4cqw centreline; measured in the site's bold (Inter Bold / Noto Sans Ethiopic Bold, upper case, 0.06em tracking, with the real fonts) "Price reduced" is 8.74em and "Not available" 8.69em — each lost a corner of its last letter — while the pre-sync "PHOTOS COMING SOON" (12.94em) could never fit and the post-sync "PHOTOS SOON" (8.05em) does. At 5cqw the usable run is 53.0cqw (10.60em) and every word fits with at least 17 % to spare, one size for all. Fix (turn 3, `2ce74f24`): `clamp(9px, 5cqw, 20px)` with `1.4cqw 0` padding; LC-6 and PW-141 follow the numbers (PW-141's expected `0.05 × width`, floor 9, cap 20, tolerance 0.75); the rule in listing-picture.tsx's comment and docs/features/posting.md: a ribbon word is at most 14 characters AND at most 10.0em in the site's bold, measured by the supervisor when a word is added (RB-1 keeps the 14). Class: a fit computed on the band's centreline, not its clipped ends (INC-670's own correction). Status (2026-10-17): FIXED in turn 3; run 968 green on the descendant commit; the walk line of the close (the word whole at 360) awaits the operator's answer.

## INC-676 — the Flake check's verdict could not be read by the supervisor (2026-10-16; tooling — the DEC-184 workflow; found at the first dispatch)

Defect: DEC-184's workflow kept its result in the run's log and the `flake-check-report` artifact, and its brief said the verdict "is read at the run's page and its report artifact" (S248). Neither is readable from the supervisor's session: the artifact and the job log need a GitHub sign-in (the session's connection answers 403 for this repository) and the proxy refuses the log download host; the run page's annotations carry only "exit code 1". Four Flake check runs on 2026-10-16/17 were read from the operator's pasted step logs (1,006, 716, 1,010 and 1,471 lines). A second half: the run step's `--reporter=list,html` replaced the config's CI reporter list, so no `test-results/results.json` existed for the failure reporter to read. Fix (turn 5, `de5197e7`): the workflow publishes `docs/tracking/flake-check-status.md` (conclusion, the inputs, commit, run) and `docs/tracking/flake-check-last-failure.md` (the failure reporter's file, source `flake`) to branch ci-evidence through publish-evidence.sh, the nightly's way; the `--reporter` override removed; the job `contents: write`; `E2E_FLAKE_LEDGER` pointed away so the repeat (0 retries) can never write the flake ledger; a "Report test outcome" step keeps the run's cross. Class: an evidence channel assumed open without a tested read (G7; the DEC-098 class — every verdict the supervisor must read lives on branch ci-evidence). Status (2026-10-17): FIXED in turn 5; its proof is the first dispatch after turn 5 (the files appear on ci-evidence) — owed with DEC-185's clean repeats.

## INC-677 — AGENTS.md sits at the platform's size cap, so every rule the executor adds shortens existing hardened rules (2026-10-17; tooling — the executor's rulebook; found at bundle 19 turn 1's verification; second occurrence)

Defect: the executor adds an "architecture record" line to AGENTS.md on its own initiative after a turn that touches a boundary (bundle 18 turn 3: the DEC-184 line; bundle 19 turn 1: the QR boundary line) and, because the root rules outside the LOVABLE block are at the platform's cap (about 5,100 bytes), it shortens existing lines to make room ("Shortened root rules" — the "database tool" rule, 2026-10-16; "Shortened AGENTS.md text" — the constitution header, the CI-evidence "Why", the readAllPages "Why", the actionlint "Why", 2026-10-17). Both rewordings were read whole by the supervisor; the meaning held in each, but a hardened rule's wording (its incident numbers, its "Why") is what keeps it from being argued around. Class rule (G8, at two): no new AGENTS.md line unless a brief asks for it; a rule the executor wants recorded goes to docs/conventions.md or the feature's doc, named in its report; at each records turn the supervisor reads AGENTS.md whole against the versions it shortened and restores any meaning lost. Fix (turn 6, `ee15261a`): `attributeOptions` keyed by `attr_key`, `options?` optional, `pin` nullable with `?.` reads; a slug longer than 200 characters → the gone page (ad-page.ts); AV-4 corrected, AV-5/AV-6 new; the contract line in ad-page.md. Class: a mapping written from a prose contract instead of the consumer's reads (the component) and the producer's SQL; the rule: a mapping's brief names the consumer's lookup key by file:line and every nullable field of the producer by its SQL branch. Status (2026-10-17): FIXED in turn 6; on run 977 (`ee15261a`) the page rendered for a pinless ad (AP-9 reached its title and price; its red there is INC-681's) and AP-12 and AP-13 were not among the run's twelve gating failures.

## INC-679 — PW-162 part (d) did not reach its step after the simulated failed send: the test raced the app's own retry, over a product path where a late Next could still move the screen after Back (2026-10-17; wizard + test — e2e/post-wizard-pricing.spec.ts, use-draft.ts; found on run 973, both projects)

Defect: run 973 (`dbce16e8`, turns 2–4) failed PW-162 outright in both projects, both attempts: "PW-162 d: Next did not reach photos" with no summary standing — after the simulated transport failure (the first draft send aborted, the route continued), Back, Back, Next on Specifications did not reach step 2 in 20 s. Fix (turn 10 A4, `631840db`), in the product: goTo always ends the claim (a token bump even when strictRef is already null) and saveAt returns true only while its token is still current — accepted; `toSpecs` made self-describing on failure; no wait lengthened (the same turn's third change, discarding late answers, is INC-691; the earlier race at :838 is INC-682). Class: a test racing the app's own retry over a product path a late answer could still move; a diagnosis held as a hypothesis until the decisive lines were read (G3, G21/G23). Status (2026-10-17): FIXED in turn 10; run 985 (`631840db`) green on PW-162 in both projects ("the diagnostic was never needed"); it regressed on run 986 through turn 11's A0 → INC-698.

Class: a geometry read across two frames — G38 "boxes measured, nothing read while an animation runs" (INC-384's class); SC-13 already measures its rows in ONE `evaluate` (e2e/admin-screening.spec.ts :689–:703); and a wait prescribed on a state the fixture cannot reach (S258). Status (2026-10-17): FIXED in turn 10; run 979 carried it (AP-17 ×2, expected); run 985 green on AP-17. ## INC-756 — the phone rail's rows fell to 24 px once the rail could scroll (2026-10-19; page — app-rail.tsx's phone rows: compactClass :225, CategoryNav's rows :558 and :600, the nav :544 and :699 at `d30646b0`; found by run 1038)

Defect: after turn 17 every row of the phone strip and of the opened menu measured 24 px — its icon's height — instead of 32–40 px. Evidence (run 1038, 05:37:51Z; the smoke, the fast lane and shard 3): "the strip sits under the fixed bar" (shell.spec.ts :1006, "Expected: >= 31 Received: 24"), "the menu opens in place" (:1239, 24), "primary touch targets are at least 44px" (:1459, 24), and FV-1 (:3810, the strip's and the menu's rows 33.17 px apart). Read: the rows fill their list item with `h-full` — a percentage of the item's height — and an item's height is only definite while every container above it has a definite height; turn 17 made the nav `min-h-full` (a minimum, its height open-ended) so that the rail could scroll, and from then each `h-full` row resolved to its content. The items still shared the rail's height, so the operator's walk (00:56 local) saw the rows spread as before; the tap area and the highlight had shrunk to 24 px. Fix: bundle 21 turn 18 — in the phone variants every row fills its item by flex (the item a flex column, the row `flex-1`), never by a percentage height; the rail still fills when its rows fit and scrolls when they do not. Class: a percentage height under a container whose height became a minimum — a container-height change is read down to every child that sizes itself by a percentage (S309). Status (2026-10-19): FIXED in turn 18; its run judges (the strip test, "the menu opens in place", the touch-target test, FV-1, RL-1).

Identified from Organization › Usage (01:18 local): "Your grace period has started. Your organization went over its quota in the previous billing cycle (Monthly Active Users Exceeded). You can continue with your projects until your grace period ends on 31 Oct, 2026. After that, the Fair Use Policy will apply … requests to your projects will return a 402 status code." The overage is the cycle before DEC-097's pool (125,442 MAU on staging, recorded 2026-10-01). This cycle (05 Oct – 05 Nov, Pro plan): MAU 26,352 / 100,000 (26%) after 15 days — ≈ 1,750 a day, ESTIMATE ≈ 54,000 by 05 Nov at that rate (under the quota); egress 66.6 / 250 GB; log ingestion 72.7 GB marked UPCOMING (shown $26.35, not billed yet); compute Small 364 h ($7.50) and Micro 364 h ($4.89). Evidence: the operator's two screenshots. Class: an organisation quota over its limit with the spend cap ON — restriction, not a bill. Risk: faster CI → more runs → more fresh accounts. Fix: D228 / DEC-209–DEC-211 — CI's tests moved to temporary backends (turn 16, DEC-214 KEEP), so tests stop counting toward the organisation's MAU and log quotas; the operator's VACUUM FULL on staging (DEC-212, done 2026-10-21). Status (2026-10-20): OPEN, watched — the MAU figure weekly until 31 Oct.

## INC-783 — AP-46 measures the Save/Share box against the title box from one read after a two-read stability poll, and the two bottoms sit 72 px apart on a first attempt (2026-10-20; test — e2e/ad-page.spec.ts AP-46 :1619, the assertion :1653–:1655 at `7bdeb9fe`; found by the supervisor's flake-ledger read)

The test waits until two consecutive box reads are equal, then reads once more and asserts; a layout that holds still for one poll interval and then moves (a late block in the title box) passes the poll and fails the read. HYPOTHESIS (G3 addendum) until the snapshot is read for which block arrived late. Fix: owed to the flake-and-cleanup turn — find the late block, wait on its own truth, then assert the same 24 px rule; no tolerance change; proven by the Flake check (DEC-184). Class: a stability poll of two equal reads is not proof the layout is final (G38). Status (2026-10-22): OPEN — AP-46 at three lines in the 7-day ledger of 2026-10-21; not among the incidents DEC-234 closed as contention.

## INC-786 — the view counter's insert fails with a foreign-key error when the listing is deleted while it is viewed (2026-10-20; server — /api/listings/view, table listing_counters; found by run 1061's server census, shard 1)

Defect: "[ssr-error] /api/listings/view insert or update on table "listing_counters" violates foreign key constraint "listing_counters_listing_id_fkey"" — a view of a listing that was deleted between the page and the beacon (a test's teardown beside AP-35 / AT-51) reaches the server as a 5xx-class error instead of "listing gone". Evidence: run 1061 e2e-last-failure.md, server census, 1 line. Fix: owed to the flake-and-cleanup turn — the view door treats a missing listing (the foreign-key refusal, SQLSTATE 23503) as the same quiet outcome as a listing not found, with a test that deletes the listing before the beacon; census (G29) of every door that writes a row keyed by listing_id after a read. Class: a write keyed by a row another actor can delete must treat the delete as a state, not an error. Status (2026-10-22): OPEN — the same server line appeared in the Flake check of 2026-10-22 (run 39713645937, staging, 8 workers; the route logs it and answers {counted:false} 200) and the counter doors' read-then-insert race was registered as INC-821.

## INC-787 — main cannot be promoted: GitHub refuses the promote job's push of a range that adds a workflow file (2026-10-20; CI — .github/workflows/ci.yml promote job :1178-:1193; found by run 1062)

Defect: run 1062 (7464c799) passed every test, and its promote job failed: "refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow `.github/workflows/local-backend-proof.yml` without `workflows` permission". The job pushes with the workflow's GITHUB_TOKEN (contents: write), which has no `workflows` permission; turn 14 added the proof workflow, so main (38b9e6d6) cannot fast-forward while the range carries it, and every run ends FAILURE by promote alone. The same kind of push succeeded on 2026-10-17 (run 969, flake-check.yml); why it is refused now is unknown (HYPOTHESIS: a GitHub-side enforcement change). Evidence: guards-last-failure.md of run 1062 (the promote job's tail). Fix: a credential with the `workflows` permission for the promote job only — the operator's decision (a security trade-off, G17) → DEC-210: the fine-grained token PROMOTE_TOKEN (Contents and Workflows read/write, this repository only, expiry 90 days), wired in turn 14e (`3f064e01`) for promote and sync-main, with a first step that fails by name on an empty secret and no fall-back. Class: a job that pushes code must hold every permission the pushed range can need, including workflow files. Status (2026-10-20): CLOSED — run 1065's promote job wrote main with PROMOTE_TOKEN (main = `3f064e01`; DEC-210 proven).

## INC-788 — two readers of the category tree on one page can hold different versions: each mount keeps its own copy (2026-10-20; product — src/features/categories/category-tree.ts useCategoryTree :400-:434, loadCategoryTree :291-:305 at `3f064e01`; found by the Flake check's diagnosis (turn 14c's rowPair), run 39392539925)

Defect: useCategoryTree holds the tree in per-mount state; a mount made later (the phone menu, opened after the strip) revalidates and sees a newer catalogue while earlier mounts keep the older copy; nothing tells them. Evidence: the Flake check's failure bodies — the strip and the menu list different scratch categories (19 vs 18, 17 vs 19 rows), so flex-filled row heights differ (32 vs 32.83, 35.06 vs 32 px) and the offset grows down the list (INC-773 FV-1, INC-784 RM-1, "the menu opens in place"). A product defect, not a test defect: two readers on one page can show different versions of the catalogue, and the same holds for every consumer (feed, cards, crumbs, wizard, admin pages). Fix: one shared, subscribed store for the held tree (every mount asks; every mount sees the newest version; same object when unmoved); unit test (two mounts; the later one's revalidation updates the earlier one), shown red against the current code; then the Flake check of the three tests. Built in turn 15 (`244b1e71`): a module-level reader set with subscribe; loadCategoryTree notifies the readers when the held object changes; useCategoryTree reads `useSyncExternalStore`; per-mount isLoading/error and the every-mount revalidation kept; fourteen call sites (the executor corrected the brief's "fifteen" — S342) and useCurrencies unchanged; the AGENTS.md rule added. Class: a value shared across a page is held in one store that every reader subscribes to, never copied into each reader's state. Status (2026-10-20): FIXED in turn 15 (`244b1e71`); run 1066 SUCCESS; Flake check 7 (run 39407106701): every row-level assertion passed in 72 — INC-773 and INC-784 CLOSED by this fix.

## INC-789 — the temporary backend's API answered over http, and the app keeps only https photo links: every stored photo read as "no photo" (2026-10-20; harness — .github/workflows/local-backend-proof.yml; found by proof #7, 13 tests, both projects)

Defect: the CLI serves the local API at http://127.0.0.1:54321; the app's photo readers keep a link only when it begins "https://" (photo-links.ts :29 and :43 at `78b96e25`, a product rule: no http image on an https site), so every signed link was dropped: the gallery drew no thumbnails (AP-9, AP-48), no main photo (AP-36, AP-50, PP-22, PP-23), the card read "No photo yet" (FS-15, PP-21), the photo step drew nothing and its Edit button stayed disabled (PP-12, PP-27, PP-28), and the two tests that read the link printed it (AP-19, AP-49). Class: an environment that differs from production in a property the product relies on — fixed in the environment, never by relaxing the product rule or a test. Fix (turn 15c B): a per-run certificate authority made in the job (its key deleted once the API certificate is signed); the CLI's own TLS for the API (`[api.tls]` with cert_path and key_path, CLI 2.120.0 pkg/config — the external URL becomes https); Chromium trusts the CA through the runner's NSS database ($HOME/.pki/nssdb) and Node and Bun through NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS; the three exact-URL guards (the workflow's status parse :301, e2e/global-setup.ts :405, e2e/helpers/app-target.ts :18-:19 with src/test/app-target.test.ts) accept https://127.0.0.1:54321 only. Grounding (the supervisor's workspace, 11:3xZ): Node 22 and Bun 1.3.14 refuse the private CA without the variable (UNABLE_TO_VERIFY_LEAF_SIGNATURE) and accept it with it; Playwright's Chromium build 1194 (headless shell and full) refuses it with no trust (ERR_CERT_AUTHORITY_INVALID) and with the CA in the NSS database loads the page, an image from an http page and APIRequestContext all 200, with no ignore flag. Status (2026-10-20): FIXED in turn 15c (`6baac306`); proven on proof #8 ("API: https://127.0.0.1:54321 (per-run certificate authority)"; the photo tests green).

## INC-790 — the languages page judged a language's publication by its own rows, not by the base catalogue: a language with no rows read publishable while the door refuses (2026-10-20; product — src/features/admin/translations/languages-page.tsx coverageOf :176-:180, the public cell :501-:509 at `78b96e25`; found by proof #7, TR-6 both projects)

Defect: the door (admin_set_language_flags, 20260901234603) refuses publication unless the language holds an approved, non-null row for every live key of the BASE catalogue; the page's gate computes remaining = (the language's own live rows) − (its approved rows). A language holding no rows (never synced for it — om on the temporary backend, where only the scratch key's en and am rows exist) reads 0 of 0, its switch is enabled, and the click is refused by the door. Staging hides it: its sync wrote om's 2,938 untranslated rows. Class: a completeness judgement measured over the wrong universe — the EMPTY-SET LAW (INC-095h) applied to the base catalogue but not to a language's own rows. Fix (turn 15c C): one pure judgement beside TranslationStats — every non-base language measured against the base catalogue's live keys (total = base, approved capped at base, remaining = base − approved); the gate and both meters read it; the base language keeps its own (`coverageAgainstBase` in translations-service.ts; four unit cases, case 1 shown red with the own-rows formula). Residual, named: the stats count an approved row with a null value as approved where the door does not. Status (2026-10-20): FIXED in turn 15c (`6baac306`); proven on proof #8 (TR-6 green).

## INC-791 — PW-162 (d): a Next's claim went out twice in one press again — a save run queued before the Next carried it (2026-10-20; product — src/features/posting/use-draft.ts flush :479-:492, the follow-up timer :380-:390, every run queued from a timer or a change; found by proof #7, both projects)

Defect: (d) aborts the first step-4 send; the evidence shows sends [step 2 sent, step 4 aborted, step 4 sent, step 4 sent] and the wizard on step 5 — the claim was sent twice and the second send advanced it. HYPOTHESIS (G3; the queue read verbatim at `78b96e25`, the timing not visible): a run queued BEFORE the Next — the 0-ms follow-up timer armed by an autosave answered before the press (:387-:389), or a debounce, change, retry or pause run waiting behind an in-flight save — reaches the queue first after the press; `pass` reads strictRef and carries the claim; its transport failure is not charged to the claim, and the Next's own run sends it again; a follow-up flag set in a run's last pass also outlives that run (flush :482 checks once). INC-698 closed one path (a superseded answer armed nothing); this is the class at its second occurrence. Fix (turn 15c D): every run notes the claim count when it is queued and sends nothing when a newer claim was made since; follow-ups are drained inside the run that got the answer (no 0-ms timer); both shown red-first in unit cases with positive controls (red at the base "expected undefined to be false", sends [1,1,5,5] and [1,5,5]; 20/20 after). Class rule (AGENTS.md, turn 15c): a run armed before a Next never carries it. Status (2026-10-20): FIXED in turn 15c (`6baac306`); proven on proof #8 (PW-162 green).

## INC-792 — the attributes import spec outpaces the door's per-user preview budget on a faster backend (2026-10-20; harness — e2e/admin-attributes-import.spec.ts importPost :107-:123 and the other preview senders; found by proof #7: AT-27 failed, AT-70 and AT-71 retried, all 429 tooManyRequests)

Status (2026-10-20): FIXED in turn 15c (`6baac306`); proven on proof #8 (the AT import tests green).

## INC-794 — the proof lane masked its results file as raw text, and the e-mail rule broke the JSON: lane 3's failure body was lost (2026-10-20; harness — .github/workflows/local-backend-proof.yml step "Write lane evidence" :557-:559 at `6baac306`; found by proof #8, lane 3)

Defect: after counting from test-results/results.json, the step rewrites it with `artifact.write_text(redact(artifact.read_text(errors='replace')))`; redact's e-mail rule `[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}` also matches the letter of a JSON escape before an address: `"line\nuser@example.invalid"` becomes `"line\[e-mail]"`, an invalid escape. Proven in the supervisor's workspace (Python: "Invalid \escape: line 1 column 12"). The render-leak error carries 2,000 characters of the page's text (e2e/helpers/ui.ts :156), and the staff ad page shows the seller's e-mail on its own line, so LGC-3's failure body is exactly the breaking input; the lane's own counts were right because Python parsed the file before masking it; turn 15b made the masked file the reporter's input. Class: a text-level mask applied to a structured file. Fix (turn 15d): the results file is masked as data — every string value and key redacted, the file written back with json.dumps — with a self-check on a synthetic escape-before-address string; census of every mask over a structured file (G29) — six masks, the results file the only structured one. Status (2026-10-20): FIXED in turn 15d (`643b49b6`); proven on proof #9 ("Sources without results: none").

## INC-795 — the staff ad page renders “undefined” while it loads on the temporary backend (LGC-3, 3 of 4 proofs) (2026-10-20; product — /admin/listings/<id>, src/features/admin-listings/listing-page.tsx whatOf :277-:287 and en.ts admin.listings.status.\* :937-:945 at `17e867e2`; found by proofs #6, #8, #9)

Defect: LGC-3's gotoReady on /admin/listings/<id> fails the render invariant with a standalone "undefined" in the page text; green on staging and in proof #7; intermittent on the temporary backend (fails at 360 or 1280, sometimes passes on retry). Diagnosed once INC-796's guard named the element (proof #10: "rendered “undefined” at listing-history-what < listing-history-entry-0 < listing-history (p): “Status: undefined → Waiting for review”"): the staff ad page's history summarizes the publish as a state entry draft → screening (history.ts `summarize` :112-:119); `whatOf` prints `t("admin.listings.history.status")` with `{from}` = `statusLabel("draft")` = `t("admin.listings.status.draft")`; en.ts has admin.listings.status.\* for active, reduced, screening, held, expired, sold, rejected, removed and closed — no draft — and `t` is `messages[key] ?? en[key]`, so a key in neither catalogue returns undefined and `.replace` prints "undefined". A real product defect on production too: every published ad's staff history read "Status: undefined → Waiting for review". Why staging passes and the temporary backend fails three times in four: the history is its own query, and the guard reads the page at gotoReady — on staging the history has not arrived yet, on the faster backend it often has (the timing, not the defect, differs). Evidence: INC-796. Fix (turn 15f): the key admin.listings.status.draft, en "Draft", am "ረቂቅ" (U+1228 U+1242 U+1245 — the approved text of myListings.status.draft and admin.legal.status.draft, copied by key); a red-first case in history.test.ts reading the ten statuses of listings_status_check (20261014194317 :49-:50) and expecting each en and am label; a census of the 37 dynamic-key calls of t (every closed set covered after the fix; one open site → INC-799). Class: a dynamic translation key whose value set is not covered by the catalogue (G29 census of every dynamic key). Status (2026-10-20): FIXED in turn 15f (`1a5b21bd`); proven on proof #11 (LGC-3 green in both projects); run 1071 SUCCESS.

## INC-800 — a new high advisory in the dev-server chain turned the dependency audit red (2026-10-20; dependencies — package.json :114 vite ^8.0.16, launch-editor 2.14.1 via @tanstack/devtools-vite; found by run 1073)

## INC-812 — the account of anyone who published, or drafted, a legal version can never be deleted (2026-10-21; Tier A — account deletion, a privacy right — legal_versions.published_by / created_by (M1 20261019063500 :56-:57) and the finality trigger (M1 :151-:153); found by the supervisor while grounding turn 20, reproduced on a scratch PostgreSQL 16)

Fix (turn 20): M16 re-declares legal_versions_finality whole from M1 :142-:165 with one change (an UPDATE of a published version that only sets published_by and/or created_by to NULL passes); the new legal_reviews table is built with the same rule; E2E proof: a fresh account that published a scratch version is deleted and the version's published_by reads NULL. ## INC-943 — the browser install's 300-second deadline was set without measuring, below the install's normal slow tail, and its retry after a cut-off cannot succeed (2026-10-27 14:4xZ; turn 34e's first run)

Defect: turn 34e's brief gave `bunx playwright install --with-deps chromium` 300 s a try and one retry. The figure was not measured: over 371 lane runs (2026-10-25 → 10-27; the Actions API's step times) the install took 14 s at the median, 582 s at the 90th percentile, 809 s at the 99th and 895 s at most — 66 of the 371 (18%) past 300 s, each of which passed slowly before turn 34e. On run 40519893778 (`a308c6b3`) lanes 3, 5 and 12 ran past 300 s on their first try and failed at once on the second (`ci-deadline … failed with exit 1 on try 2 of 2`); one lane passed on its retry. The second try's error is not in the evidence the supervisor can read (the job logs need a sign-in); the reading — a package install cut off part-way leaves the system's package manager interrupted — is a hypothesis consistent with the retry that passed (cut off in its download, after the libraries were in). Evidence: the run's annotations (`ci-retry` and `ci-deadline` on lanes 3, 5 and 12); local-backend-proof.md on ci-evidence for the run ("not run" for lanes 3, 5, 12); the step-time census above. Fix (records turn R5, Part B; DEC-276): the system libraries (`bunx playwright install-deps chromium`) once with 1500 s, the browser download (`bunx playwright install chromium`) with 900 s a try and one retry, in all five installs (local-backend-proof.yml, nightly-e2e.yml ×2, flake-check.yml, guard-proof.yml); the certificate tools' `apt-get install` once with 600 s; CF-CID-1's fifth rule (a package install runs once) with its planted breach in CF-CID-2, red first on `a308c6b3` (six findings). Class: concern "every CI job and every outside call carries a deadline" — a deadline is a measurement, not a guess, and a retry only where re-running is safe; mechanism scripts/ci/with-deadline.sh and CF-CID (register row 59). Status (2026-10-27): FIXED in records turn R5 — closes on DEC-276's judge.

## INC-967 — the repeat lane cannot repeat a helper's change: a changed e2e helper selects nearly every spec (2026-10-28; turn C2's stop-4 run)

Defect: on run 40713967683 (`f18cb06`) the repeat lane (DEC-283) selected 1,074 tests because a changed e2e helper is imported by nearly every spec, and repeated 18 of them (the rest "not repeated"); the specs the turn changed directly were not preferred over the helper's importers. Fix: the selector ranks the spec files a push changes directly before the specs that import a changed helper, and a helper's own unit tests carry its repeatability; the lane's evidence names how many directly changed specs it repeated. Class: concern "every changed browser test is repeated inside the normal CI run"; mechanism the repeat lane and scripts/e2e-select.ts --repeat. Status (2026-10-28): OPEN — the next Lovable turn, with INC-966.

## INC-968 — an md5(prosrc) proof is not portable across the hand-apply path (2026-10-29; Foundations turn D1, stop 12)

Defect: the operator's SQL Editor turns LF into CRLF, so a proof that fingerprints a function body with md5(prosrc) fails on ethio-staging for code that is the same. Fix (landed in D1): every body fingerprint is md5(replace(prosrc, E'\r', '')), expected hashes computed the same way; the rule lives in docs/features/ci-guards.md. Status (2026-10-29): FIXED.

## INC-970 — a landed proof read real published legal versions, so the temporary backend's replay dies at M4 (2026-10-29; Foundations turn D1, red board)

Defect (Tier A; a real row in a proof, G27 addendum; banned pattern "Real rows in a proof"): M4's proof (20261028230748_23f4ae4e) SELECTed two real published in-force legal_versions and RAISEd 'two versions in force are needed' when absent; a fresh backend has none, the replay raised, and all nineteen E2E lanes failed with zero tests from 573368b on. Proven by reading: countries/currencies/languages/roles are seeded by earlier migrations (M1/M2/M5a/M5b's seeded reads replay), legal_versions is not. Fix (option a of the ruling): the proof creates its own scratch document and two published versions (the M13/M14/M16 pattern); function bodies byte-identical, only the proof's DO block changed; prod and staging are not re-applied (the proof is not state). New file sha256 049423b32d8c79ccc0af67fd4e5a7792872d2920ec57a4e4627fc7127e57a4fe. The scratch inserts were validated against the live constraints and triggers on ethio-prod in a rolled-back statement. Census (every D1 file's proof block): M1 :21 and M2 :24 read seeded countries (replay-safe), M5a :105-106 and M5b :57-58 read seeded languages (replay-safe), M4 read real legal_versions (the killer, fixed), M3/M3b/M4b/M6a/M6b-legal/cat1/cat2a/cat2b/M6c-1 create their own rows or read seeded roles only. Rule for the M6c/M7 files: their proofs create every row they read. Status (2026-10-29): FIXED on dev; CI is the judge.

## INC-973 — a failed backend start reaches the evidence as only "log unavailable" (2026-10-29; Foundations turn D1, red board)

Defect (evidence gap, the self-report law): when the temporary backend fails to start, every lane dies before tests, no results or lane log is uploaded, and local-backend-last-failure.md (scripts/e2e-failure-report.ts over the lane artifacts) can only say "log unavailable"; the start log never reaches the evidence branch. Fix: the lane's evidence step writes local-backend-start-failure.txt (the failing migration's name + the last twenty ERROR/FATAL lines, redacted like the rest) into the e2e-log artifact; the reporter reads it (Source.startFailure) and renders a "## Backend start failure (INC-973)" section — one lane's lines, named, standing for every lane that failed the same way. Planted self-test: a source with startFailure lines renders the section (proven red when the section is removed), a source without keeps the bare gap. Status (2026-10-29): FIXED on dev; CI is the judge.

## INC-975 — the secrets scan walked a push with `--no-merges --first-parent`, so commits reaching dev through the platform's merges were never scanned (2026-10-29 04:18Z; CI run 40812371557 on 5f2c5396)

Defect: gitleaks-action@v3 scans a push as `--no-merges --first-parent before^..after`. Every platform commit on dev is a merge, so the run on 5f2c5396 scanned 0 commits, and c7bb093a..14045945 scans 0 of its 31. Evidence: the run's log ("0 commits scanned"); a local replay with gitleaks 8.24.3: 0 → 2 commits on 4819f7cc..5f2c5396, 0 → 31 on c7bb093a..14045945. Fix: the CI step runs pinned gitleaks over `origin/main..HEAD` with `--diff-merges=first-parent`, the commits not yet promoted, merges included. main advances only on green (DEC-020), so no commit reaches main unscanned, and a cancelled run loses nothing. Class: an outside tool's default scope taken on trust (concern: CI evidence covers what it claims; mechanism: the secrets-scan job, docs/features/ci-guards.md). Status (2026-10-29): CLOSED in Foundations turn A2. Note: the same replay over history already on main (81bd4625..HEAD, 6,617 commits) shows 39 generic-api-key hits in 16 places: attribute and translation key names in migrations, a changelog line and e2e-last-failure lines. None is a secret, all sit on main, and they are outside the new range. Listed in the A2 report, not ignored.

## INC-976 — the gitleaks action's own artifact upload had no deadline (2026-10-29 04:18Z; CI run 40812371557)

Defect: after "no leaks found", the action's SARIF artifact upload failed (`FinalizeArtifact … ETIMEDOUT`) and failed the job: an outside call with no deadline or retry (INC-935's class). Fix: the action is replaced by a pinned, SHA-256-checked gitleaks download through scripts/ci/with-deadline.sh. The verdict is the exit code; no artifact is uploaded, and the log carries counts only. `GITLEAKS_ENABLE_UPLOAD_ARTIFACT` no longer applies because the action is gone, and INC-975 needs the range the action cannot take. Class: every outside call in CI carries a deadline (CF-CID-1, INC-935). Status (2026-10-29): CLOSED in Foundations turn A2.

## INC-977 — a seller name saved unchecked while the AI check was unavailable is never AI-checked later (2026-10-29 04:18Z; turn A2's plan)

Defect: when name_check answers `unavailable`, identity.ts saves the name and writes `alias.unchecked` (src/routes/api/listings/identity.ts:89, D158). Nothing in src/ or supabase/migrations/ reads that action, and seller_name_sweep() (20261004011235_18556a32…sql:1100) counts only the rule check `alias_rule(..., false)`. So an unchecked name is never AI-checked. Evidence: the A2 plan census (rg over src and migrations). Fix: its own turn after INC-974, plan first. Class: a degraded path without its catch-up (concern: an identity imitation check; mechanism: identity.ts + the seller-name sweep). Status (2026-10-29): OPEN.
